sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Satnami Sect**: Founded by **Guru Ghasidas** in the early 19th century (c. 1820s) in the Chhattisgarh region, focusing on the worship of 'Satnam' (True Name).
• **Egalitarian Philosophy**: Explicit rejection of the **caste-based hierarchy** and idol worship, promoting the concept of 'Manavta' (Humanity) and equality of all beings.
• **Social Reform**: Advocated for **abstinence** from intoxicants, non-violence, and the dignity of labor, which served as a catalyst for the socio-economic upliftment of the marginalized communities (Satnamis).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement acted as a **subaltern resistance** against the feudal and colonial structures of the Central Provinces.

items.definition: The 'True Name' of the formless God; central to the sect's theology, emphasizing direct connection with the divine without priestly mediation.
A white pillar erected at the center of Satnami villages, symbolizing the victory of truth and the presence of the divine; a key cultural marker of the sect.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Social Empowerment**: The movement provided a distinct identity to the Dalit communities, fostering self-respect and collective bargaining power.
• **Cultural Identity**: Preservation of unique rituals and the 'Jaitkhamb' tradition as a symbol of resistance against social exclusion.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Historical suppression by feudal landlords and colonial authorities; internal fragmentation over time.
• **Solutions**: Institutionalizing the legacy through state-sponsored cultural centers and academic research on subaltern history.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'G-S-C' (Ghasidas - Satnami - Chhattisgarh).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Ghasidas founded the Satnami sect in Chhattisgarh, focusing on equality.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: Do not confuse the 19th-century Satnami movement of Guru Ghasidas with the 17th-century Satnami revolt against Aurangzeb. They share a name but are distinct historical events.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Agency' when discussing Guru Ghasidas to highlight how marginalized groups utilized religious reform to challenge socio-political hegemony.

keyTakeaways: Guru Ghasidas was a 19th-century reformer who established the Satnami sect in Chhattisgarh.
The movement emphasized monotheism (Satnam) and rejected caste-based discrimination.
The 'Jaitkhamb' is the primary symbolic representation of the Satnami faith.
